rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a key design choice: multimodal fusion. This configuration tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, which isolates the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploration of the most promising direction (multimodal) while using standard encoders to minimize confounding factors.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and concat fusion achieve 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of changing fusion from concat to weighted, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It is a logical extension of the previous configuration, balancing exploitation of promising multimodal directions with refinement of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with concat fusion (config_016) achieve 0.526 accuracy, slightly better than weighted fusion (config_017). This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, a logical extension to evaluate if profile settings and aggregation methods improve performance. It clarifies whether multiprofile configurations could outperform singleprofile, addressing a key design choice with minimal changes to the proven RNA/image encoder pair.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with avgpool aggregation (config_018, 0.618 accuracy) outperform singleprofile configurations. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other parameters identical) can further improve performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy in the promising multiprofile/avgpool setup, balancing exploitation of strong evidence with exploration of critical design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping other components (pca_n2000 RNA encoder, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) consistent. This isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, which is a critical design decision. Testing a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) could further improve performance, leveraging the strong foundation of the current best configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. This balances exploitation of the current promising direction with exploration of a potentially better encoder, maximizing the chance of improving accuracy within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and weighted fusion with avgpool aggregation (config_031) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, isolating the effect of aggregation method. This is a logical extension of the current promising direction and could either confirm or refute the importance of transformer aggregation, providing clearer insights with limited remaining experiments.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (config_032) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_033) could further improve performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. With only 2 experiments remaining, this comparison directly addresses a critical design choice with potential to enhance accuracy.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_033) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a more powerful vision model) while maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance. This comparison isolates the impact of the image encoder, a critical design choice, and leverages the strong prior evidence for transformer aggregation and weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests replacing scvi_n200 RNA encoder with scgpt (a more advanced encoder) while retaining the proven aggregation/fusion strategy. It directly addresses whether upgrading the RNA encoder can further improve performance, leveraging strong prior evidence for the aggregation/fusion combination.
